report.review_type: independent qualitative inspection of all eight preset extra cases after source freeze
report.qa_crop_note: Each crop stacks original, candidates and final at the same display coordinates. The crop is a diagnostic view only; it is not passed into prediction or used as a manual prompt.
report.overall: On these eight additional open-development examples the clear free segment and most of the oblique crossing are broadly followed. Guide interruptions are bridged without the old guide-top detour. This is not proof of complete dark-side same-rope recovery: several final tails are orange or terminate early, local center/edge displacement remains, and candidate divergence is visible. No earlier identical-parameter run of these extra cases was reviewed, so these observations do not provide a numerical or matched-case net-gain estimate.

cases.observed: The long visible wire from the right guide toward the top-left coil region is broadly followed; the handheld tool at lower left is not selected. The guide gap is orange. Candidate lines separate near the left end.
cases.remaining: Terminal left sections alternate green/orange near the top surface and flange. Center alignment may favor an edge/shadow. The last left-side turn and disappearance are not uniquely confirmed.

cases.observed: The long diagonal crossing and guide reappearance are recovered. The selected candidate does not take the much steeper gray alternative down across the coil.
cases.remaining: The left dark tail becomes orange and flattens toward the visible side. The image does not establish that its final old-row association is correct. Guide bridging is inferred, not observed through the obstruction.

cases.observed: The selected path follows the thin rope from the upper right toward the top-left surface, while avoiding the much thicker bright handheld tool. This is a useful qualitative separation of rope and tool for this entry.
cases.remaining: The path terminates near the gloved-hand/top-surface region. Once the wire merges into the upper coil contour, the dark endpoint cannot be independently assigned to a unique same-root turn. The orange endpoint is appropriately unconfirmed.

cases.observed: The clear diagonal from left to the spool is broadly recovered. The main candidate is smoother than the visibly lower cyan alternative in the exterior-to-surface region.
cases.remaining: The right dark tail is orange and remains relatively flat, reaching near or slightly past the visible right boundary. There is no independent evidence that it follows the full last bend. Local center and shadow-edge distinction remain approximate.

cases.observed: The free segment and broad oblique crossing are recovered, and the chosen curve turns gradually toward the dark right side rather than selecting the steep magenta alternative.
cases.remaining: Near the bright band exit, the selected line appears slightly above the dark central boundary of the visible rope, flattening before the terminal bend. This is a potential local displacement even though nearby pixels are green. The orange dark bend cannot be certified as the true same-rope track.

cases.observed: The exterior rope, guide reappearance and bright crossing are broadly followed. Candidate divergence at the left end is retained.
cases.remaining: The selected path terminates near the bright-to-dark left transition while a darker continuation toward the visible side may remain. No complete curved-side disappearance is recovered. A short orange section also occurs where the exterior rope changes appearance.

cases.observed: The diagonal across the top part of the surface is followed and the main path avoids the steep magenta route through multiple lower rows. The guide gap is separately orange.
cases.remaining: Two shallow candidates differ in the dark left tail. The selected orange continuation flattens near the visible side, where individual rows are hard to separate. Same-rope identity of the terminal curve is unresolved.

cases.observed: The visible long diagonal is broadly followed, and the selected output avoids the conspicuously steep cyan branch that would cross many coil rows.

report.conclusion: Useful recovery of visible long segments on the extra set, with retained endpoint uncertainty and visible local errors. The frozen result should be delivered as a candidate-based research output, not complete validated whole-rope segmentation.
report.evaluation_limit: No target masks or independent full-endpoint labels were read. The green/orange color, path length, absence of runtime errors and avoided gross detours are not substitutes for identity accuracy. Review did not tune frozen code or parameters.

report.conclusion: Pilot 001 is not ready as a whole-rope result. Several clear guide-induced deviations and early old-row turns remain; green local support does not prevent gross identity errors. Candidate generation must recover the visible collinear segment beyond the guide before free bending.

cases.finding: Outside straight section and much of the bright-spool crossing broadly coincide with the visible rope. Small central zigzag/bump and premature dark-tail termination remain. This is a partial alignment observation, not full-root confirmation.

Fusion candidates bend toward a near-horizontal old row immediately after reaching the bright band, visibly above the still-oblique active rope. Both green and cyan fusion alternatives are wrong at that turn. Gray heat-only candidate continues substantially farther along the visible oblique rope. This is a visible fusion regression in the candidate pool.

Only the outermost right straight segment is followed; the path bends upward along the black guide and stops. The long visible collinear segment left of the guide and over the spool is missed. Gray baseline also takes a long erroneous route over the upper spool boundary, so merely switching to heat-only would not fix this case.

Fusion turns at the guide and stops before the long visible crossing. Gray heat-only path recovers much of the visible segment left of the guide but bends around the occluder instead of distinguishing a hidden gap; it cannot be promoted wholesale as observed rope.

Entry 1 starts on the metal tool and climbs onto the upper spool edge, producing a long false green ribbon. Entry 2 starts on the actual outer rope but turns upward around the guide and follows upper spool/flange edges. Both outputs contain large clearly wrong green portions. The tool entry requires independent rejection/explicit invalid-entry labeling; it is not an ambiguous continuation of the actual rope.

Most exterior and bright-spool oblique section aligns with the visible rope. The final downward turn is too early/steep relative to the visible oblique continuation and traverses old-row texture. Gray baseline turns later but is not independently confirmed either. Tail should not be called full-rope recovery.

Fusion bends upward at the guide, follows the upper spool edge, then makes a nearly vertical descent through multiple wound rows. This is a major incorrect route despite extensive green local-support marking. Gray baseline is closer to the crossing but still routes around the guide.
Most visible long oblique section is broadly aligned. A central small kink and weak/short dark tail remain. The final tail does not establish complete same-root identity.

candidate_repairs: Use the original straight-axis prediction to search for collinear reappearance beyond a weak/occluded gap; require compatible width, paired original edges and repeated strand evidence over a sustained segment. Keep the intervening gap unobserved rather than drawing a bent route on the guide.
During weak evidence keep the pre-gap straight direction; do not let a succession of strong guide/flange edges select a new direction.
Retain heat-only and straight continuation as independent candidates alongside fusion, then evaluate all by the same image tests. Lf142 shows the fusion pool can lose a visibly better baseline path.

Bound turn per unit arc length more tightly than unrestricted 6 degrees per 6 processing pixels. Within these fixed camera views, test a gradual downward-turn preference to prevent hooks upward onto the guide/top spool; this is a candidate prior, not proof of contact.
Delay F3 attraction until a supported gradual bend, and keep the near-horizontal old row from winning solely because its texture is stronger.
Preserve input-invalid, local supported, gap inference and unresolved tail states separately in mask and display. A green pixel from local scores is not a same-rope guarantee.

report.scope: 7 original open-development images, 8 B entry-conditioned views; no labels or reserved data read
common_observations: B has strong yellow/green response over broad black background and narrow responses on hardware/flange edges; absolute high response is not a target-identity test.

The free rope frequently appears as a blue narrow band with two yellow/red boundaries, whereas the same projected rope over bright spool often appears as a narrow yellow/orange ridge. Response polarity and cross-profile shape change with background.
All or most neighboring wound-rope rows also respond in the dark side regions. A visible rope-shaped trace in B does not determine which old row continues the same rope.

The 0075 tool and active-rope entry-conditioned views are visually very similar over the whole frame; this observation is not a numerical equality assertion. The old tool seed must not be promoted to confirmed rope just because B has a coherent trace there.
Fine strands produce local waviness. Mild lengthwise aggregation should be used before tracing; large dilation can fuse neighboring rows.

cases.observations: Clear diagonal free rope from left toward lower-right spool. B represents the exterior straight segment chiefly by two bright rails around a dark strip; on bright spool it becomes a bright slanted trace. Dense old-row responses on far right limit unique continuation. Background and image-border responses are far stronger in area than rope.
cases.recommendation: Use automatic straight axis/width, track a paired-profile center through the polarity change, and keep competing far-side row continuations rather than global maximum.

cases.observations: Same general geometry as f15. B clearly distinguishes the slanted crossing from old nearly horizontal rows in the central bright area, but its slanted trace has small stair-step/strand interruptions. Far-right convergence with ordinary rows is ambiguous visually.
cases.recommendation: Combine direction continuity with short-gap bridging supported by the original; do not use gap length alone to assert identity.

cases.observations: Rope runs from upper-right toward lower-left and is physically occluded by the black guide near the right. B shows both visible sides of that guide but also a broad guide outline. On the bright spool the oblique trace is recognizable; on dark left it joins a dense set of old rows.
cases.recommendation: Keep guide occlusion separate from observed mask. Reacquire collinear segment on its other side, then allow gradual bend only with local data support. Do not fill guide silhouette as rope.

cases.observations: The lower-left handheld tool creates a long diagonal response, while the actual rope is the separate upper-right-to-center diagonal. Both entry-conditioned B images have essentially the same visible competing structures. Original image shows a wider nonperiodic metal tool and hand, unlike the narrow rope with repeated strands.
cases.recommendation: Use A7/appearance validation to reject the tool entry. Keep all accepted rope entry hypotheses separate; do not merge B maps across tool and rope prompts.

cases.observations: Larger spool. Clear actual rope crosses diagonally down-left from the right guide. B has a thin bright crossing on the spool, a double-rail exterior, and strong dense adjacent-row responses at the left side. The guide creates a long discontinuity between visible free portions.
cases.recommendation: Expect response-profile changes without changing the physical width abruptly. A nearby F3 row can constrain tangent after a bend but cannot select the identity by nearest distance alone.

cases.observations: Long rope enters from the left image edge and crosses the spool toward the lower-right. B makes the exterior double edges conspicuous and the center-spool diagonal quite continuous. On the extreme right the rope's apparent trace blends with parallel wound-rope responses. Flange reflections also form strong long curves.
cases.recommendation: This is a useful straight-to-spool positive mechanism case, with far-side ambiguity retained. Constrain search to a plausible sweep from the entry rather than broad connected components.

cases.observations: The rope is visible on both sides of the black guide and over the center bright spool. B emphasizes a largely coherent oblique structure but densely responds to ordinary rows on the left dark side; the guide creates multiple competing elongated contours.
cases.recommendation: Raw paired edges plus fixed straight width help through exterior sections. Preserve the long guide gap as unobserved. At the left turning region retain uncertainty where no unique row is visually separable.

implementation_suggestions: Use the raw numerical B response, not JPEG color inverse, for final processing.
Subtract or normalize a local low-frequency response background; extract line-like relative response rather than absolute high-response regions.
Evaluate cross-sections for single central ridge and paired edges/dark valley; evaluate original grayscale edges in parallel.
Anchor from validated straight rope; bound center motion, curvature change and apparent width; use dynamic programming or a small beam with distinct lane alternatives.
Use F3 tangent/spacing only as a soft local compatibility test, not a nearest-row target selector.
Separate visible supported mask, short inferred bridges, and unresolved tails in the deliverable. A smooth complete curve alone does not validate same-rope identity.
report.limitations: This is qualitative visual diagnosis at a fixed display scale, without human target masks or endpoint identity truth; no complete-rope accuracy is reported.

known_limits: dense neighboring rows can still resemble the desired same-rope continuation
long bright/dark/occluded gaps and calculation-border responses remain possible error sources
early pilot failures and final case-specific remaining failures are preserved in the visual review reports above
no complete same-rope ground truth or independent accuracy evaluation; masks are estimated optical bands
no physical contact, true terminal point, t0/t1/t2 or production-control acceptance
